item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI‑assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description:
Anthropic mathematician claims AI‑assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced that he and the company’s AI system Claude have produced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis.

🔍 Overview

  • Claim: proof of the Riemann hypothesis with Claude.
  • Solution written in Lean, posted on Alpöge’s website.
  • Alpöge says he texted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei late Sunday night and delayed publication until after the IPO on Thursday.

🧩 Claim Details

  • Quote from Alpöge’s site: “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.”
  • He also states the method “easily extends” to the Generalized and Extended Riemann Hypotheses.
  • “Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.”

⚙️ Verification Status

  • The proof has not been independently verified.
  • Anthropic has not commented or been involved in the announcement.
  • The Verge reached out to Anthropic but did not hear back immediately.

🏅 Prize Context

  • The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, each offering a $1 million bounty.
  • Clay Mathematics Institute requires a solution to be published and to withstand at least two years of scrutiny with general acceptance before prize consideration.
  • To date, only the Poincaré conjecture has been officially solved among the prize problems.

🌐 Related AI Math Efforts

  • In August, Anthropic said it was working on the Riemann hypothesis with Claude but did not expect the techniques to lead to a proof.
  • OpenAI announced a claimed solution to the Navier‑Stokes problem, a separate Millennium problem, after hearing rumors of competing work.
  • OpenAI’s effort involved millions of dollars and 10,000 agents; the result is considered credible but lacks formal recognition and faces allegations of questionable research practices.

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims independent Riemann Hypothesis proof using Claude
item.description:
Anthropic mathematician claims independent Riemann Hypothesis proof using Claude

Within a few hours of each other, two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics. Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code rather than a full paper, while Alessandro Masullo released his 940-page, 100% human work-in-progress proof.

🧩 How it works

Levent Alpöge states that he is presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics. To avoid posting an unreadable travesty of “slop”, he decided to only present the Lean code. The artifact consists solely of Lean code, which is 1.3GB worth and equivalent to approximately 250,000 pages if written out in prose.

The work began on October 6. Eight of the 20 steps landed on November 15, and the final entry on November 16 reads “GRH.” Alpöge credits Claude for the parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups, an area where he says he has little mastery. As Alpöge noted, “Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Formalized Statement: Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).
  • Verification: Glazer puts the chance of a Lean bug at well under 1%. If the code finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, even though no human will ever have read all of it.
  • Human Alternative: Alessandro Masullo’s proof is a roughly 940-page GRH draft. It is reported as 100% human and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett for the last 12 years.
  • Uncertainties: The specific Claude model used and the degree of human steering have not been disclosed.
  • Market Reaction: ANT stock fell about 10% on the day of the announcement.

💡 Why it matters

This development is the third in a trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding. However, both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify.

OpenAI’s September Navier-Stokes claim remains a cautionary tale, as critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Artificial Analysis notes that this Riemann Hypothesis claim and the previous Navier-Stokes claim are currently unverified.

The situation highlights a distinct contrast: the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible, while the human solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable. This underscores the need for Weak to Strong alignment in the open-ended domain of controlling AI that is smarter than humans, raising questions about the No Slop Manifesto tenet that one should understand what they ship.

#RiemannHypothesis #Anthropic #FormalVerification #LeanCode #AIResearch

Source: Riemann Hypothesis proved…twice independently — Latent Space

item.title: Proposed Proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis Developed with Claude AI
item.description:
Proposed Proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis Developed with Claude AI

A proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, created by mathematician Alessandro Masullo with extensive AI assistance from Claude, has been released as a draft.

🔍 Overview

  • Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
  • The method also extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and is expected to reach the Extended Riemann Hypothesis with more time.
  • The work is entirely human‑generated, with no AI authoring the proof itself.

🧩 Collaboration with Claude

  • The author states, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.”
  • Claude and the author have formalized the arguments without assumptions.
  • The author describes Claude as having “far outpaced” them near the finish line, “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

⚙️ Current Status

  • Brian Conrad has been reviewing the draft for months, providing extensive feedback that is being incorporated.
  • The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after broader review.
  • The team decided that releasing the current draft now is the best course of action.

📅 Recent AI‑Related Activities

  • Running the full server‑side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide – 17th November 2026
  • Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude – 9th November 2026
  • Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary> – 9th November 2026
  • Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop can interpret model weights, too – 3rd November 2026
